items.stem:
Read the passage below, based on the poem 'The Tale of Melon City', and answer.

"The new gateway was finished at last, decorated with flags. The ruler rode out to admire it, and – crack! – his tall hat struck the stone and tumbled into the dust. The crowd went silent. 'Who built this?' he roared. 'Fetch the chief builder!' The chief builder bowed low. 'Your Majesty, the workmen made it.' The workmen pointed at the masons. The masons pointed at the designer."

What does each person do when asked?
items.answer: Blames someone else.
items.markingKey: Blames someone else. (1–2 marks for a complete answer.)

items.stem: Trace the chain of blame in "The Tale of Melon City". Answer in 40–50 words.
items.answer: Builders blamed workmen, workmen blamed masons, masons blamed the architect, and the architect blamed the king who had amended the plans.
items.markingKey: Value points: Builders blamed workmen, workmen blamed masons, masons blamed the architect, and the architect blamed the king who had amended the plans. (2 marks: content and expression.)

items.stem: Why do people often pass the blame instead of accepting responsibility, as seen in "The Tale of Melon City"? Answer in 40–50 words.
items.answer: Fear of punishment, pride, lack of accountability; any reasoned answer.
items.markingKey: Accept any well-reasoned answer. Value points: Fear of punishment, pride, lack of accountability; any reasoned answer. (2 marks: content and expression.)

items.stem: Narrate the events that led to the king's death in "The Tale of Melon City". Answer in about 120–150 words.
items.answer: Order for the arch; low arch; crown knocked off; order to hang builders; chain of blame; architect blames king; wise man; crowd wants hanging; noose fits only the king.
items.markingKey: Value points: Order for the arch; low arch; crown knocked off; order to hang builders; chain of blame; architect blames king; wise man; crowd wants hanging; noose fits only the king. Content 3, organisation and expression 2.
